parole.testo: From Vulgar Latin ceresia, from the neuter plural of Late Latin ceresium, from Latin cerasium, from Ancient Greek κεράσιον (kerásion, “cherry”), from Ancient Greek κερασός (kerasós, “bird cherry”), ultimately possibly of Anatolian origin.

From Old Norse fíkja, fíka. Originally either from Old English fīc or Vulgar Latin *fīca based on the -k- found in both Old Swedish and Old Icelandic, from Latin fīcus. Cognate to Old Danish fige, Danish figen, Old Swedish fīka, Swedish fikon, Old Saxon fīga, Middle Low German vīge, Middle High Germ
